questions.q: Why are the first two values of sales.rolling(3).mean() NaN?
options: The first two sales values were missing
A full window of 3 rows does not exist yet for those rows
rolling always skips the first two rows for speed
questions.explain: By default a window needs all 3 observations. Pass min_periods=1 to compute results from fewer rows at the start.

questions.q: Which pandas method is the equivalent of SQL's LAG(sales, 1)?
questions.explain: shift(1) moves values down one row so each row sees the previous row's value. shift(-1) behaves like LEAD.

A running total that restarts for each customer, with one value per original row
The number of orders per customer
questions.explain: cumsum after groupby accumulates within each group and returns a value for every row, so it is like SUM() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY ...).

questions.q: Before computing shift, diff or rolling on time-ordered data, what should you always do?
options: Sort the rows by date (and by date within each group)
questions.explain: These operations use row order, not date values. If the rows are not sorted, the results silently compare the wrong neighbors.

questions.q: For values 120 then 135, what does pct_change() return for the second row?
questions.explain: pct_change computes (135 - 120) / 120 = 0.125. The absolute difference, 15, is what diff() returns.
